'''Mary Rakowski DuBois''' is an [[inorganic chemist]], now retired from [[Pacific Northwest National Laboratory]] (PNNL).  She made multiple contributions to inorganic and organometallic chemistry, focusing on synthetic and mechanistic studies. In recognition of her scientific contributions, she received several awards.

==Education and career==
Rakowski DuBois conducted her undergraduate training at [[Creighton University]], receiving her B.S. in 1970.<ref name="CR" /> She earned her Ph.D. in 1974 under the mentorship of [[Daryle H. Busch]] at [[Ohio State University]],<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Rakowski|first=Mary Clare|url=http://rave.ohiolink.edu/etdc/view?acc_num=osu1486986122440062|title=Complexes with macrocyclic ligands: I. The oxydation reduction behavior of iron complexes. II. Synthesis and characterization of transition metal containing a pentadentate ligand|date=1974|publisher=The Ohio State University |language=English|oclc=973332814}}</ref> and then was a postdoctoral fellow with [[Earl Muetterties]] at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="CR" />

She joined the faculty of the [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado at Boulder]] in 1976, and was a professor there until 2007, where she moved to [[Pacific Northwest National Laboratory]] (PNNL).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rakowski Dubois|first1=M.|last2=Dubois|first2=Daniel L.|date=2009-12-21|title=Development of Molecular Electrocatalysts for CO2 Reduction and H2 Production/Oxidation|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ar900110c|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=42|issue=12|pages=1974–1982|doi=10.1021/ar900110c|pmid=19645445 |issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She retired from PNNL in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PNNL: Center for Molecular Electrocatalysis - Research: Reaching Out to the Next Generation of Scientist - Salmon Summit|url=https://efrc.pnnl.gov/research/rakowskidubois.asp|access-date=2021-06-08|website=efrc.pnnl.gov}}</ref>

==Research==
Together with her husband [[Daniel L. DuBois]], Rakowski DuBois led a team that elucidated the reactivity of nickel complexes of [[P2N2 ligand]]s, which were popularized at PNNL. The behavior of these complexes highlighted the strong influence of the [[second coordination sphere]] on the rates of activation of H<sub>2</sub> by 16-electron nickel complexes.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Rakowski DuBois, M. |author2=D. L. DuBois |year=2009|title=The Roles of the First And Second Coordination Spheres in the Design of Molecular Catalysts for H<sub>2</sub> Production and Oxidation|journal=Chem. Soc. Rev.|volume=38|issue=1|pages=62–72|doi=10.1039/b801197b|pmid=19088965|url=https://zenodo.org/record/1229994}}</ref>
[[File:CAZYOR.png|thumb|Structure of Cp<sub>2</sub>Mo<sub>2</sub>(S<sub>2</sub>C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>)<sub>2</sub>, prepared by the Rakowski DuBois group by addition of acetylene to Cp<sub>2</sub>Mo<sub>2</sub>S<sub>4</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Syntheses and Structures of New Molybdenum Complexes with Dithiobenzoate and Dimercaptotoluene ligands. Structural Comparisons in a Series of Dithiolate-Bridged Dimers of Molybdenum(III)|author=Warren K. Miller |author2=R. C. Haltiwanger |author3=M. C. VanDerveer |author4=M. Rokowski DuBois |journal=Inorganic Chemistry|year=1983|volume=22|issue=21|pages=2973–2979|doi=10.1021/ic00163a001}}</ref>]]
Early in her independent career, while on the faculty at the [[University of Colorado]], she discovered that organomolybdenum sulfides activated hydrogen. This work provided a mechanistic connection between the Mo-S catalysts used in [[hydrodesulfurization]] and molecular organometallic chemistry.<ref name=CR>{{cite journal|author=Rakowski DuBois, M.|year=1989|title=Catalytic Applications of Transition-Metal Complexes with Sulfide Ligands|journal=Chemical Reviews |volume=89|pages=1–9|doi=10.1021/cr00091a001}}</ref>

==Awards==
Rakowski DuBois has been honored with fellowships from Alfred P. Sloan (1981), Dreyfus (1981), and Guggenheim Foundations (1984).<ref name=CR/><ref>{{Cite web|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Mary Rakowski DuBois|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/mary-rakowski-dubois/|access-date=2021-06-08|language=en-US}}</ref>
